_comment: Tier-2 for fourc::poisson#4 — NUMDOF declares the length of ONOFF/VAL/FUNCT and is checked against them, not against the single scalar a Poisson problem transports. On a stationary TRANSP TRI3 deck, NUMDOF 1 with one-entry arrays and NUMDOF 4 with four-entry arrays (VAL [1, 2, 3, 4]) both run and return the identical centre value 5.00000000000000111e-01; the over-declared deck emits exactly one 'PROC 0 ERROR in' line, which is the deliberate recording result test (NUMDOF4_ERROR_LINES=1), so three surplus entries are dropped without comment. What IS enforced is array length == NUMDOF: NUMDOF 1 with a two-entry FUNCT is refused with "Failed to match condition specification in section 'DESIGN LINE DIRICH CONDITIONS'." from core/fem/src/condition/4C_fem_condition_definition.cpp, and 4C names the offending array — "Candidate parameter 'FUNCT' has incorrect size". Neither phrasing an earlier version of this entry quoted ('array size mismatch', 'expected NUMDOF entries') appears. Verified by execution 2026-08-06 against 4C 2026.2.0-dev (git 89519cf) at /home/alexander/4C/build/4C.
expect_in_output: Failed to match condition specification in section 'DESIGN LINE DIRICH CONDITIONS'.

_mutation.note: make the surplus entries stop being surplus: move a different value into the FIRST slot, which is the one the single scalar DOF reads. The applied boundary value changes, NUMDOF4_VALUE stops matching the NUMDOF-1 reading, and the fixture must go red — which is also what shows the comparison is sensitive to the arrays at all.
remove the pathology from the ragged arm: make FUNCT the length NUMDOF declares. The condition-spec rejection and the named-array line both disappear and the fixture must go red.
